finland/helsinki-center.name: Helsinki Senate Square, cathedral and market
finland/helsinki-center.description: The white neoclassical heart of Helsinki, with a harbour market and seafront cafes.
finland/helsinki-center.details: Senate Square has the Helsinki Cathedral at the top of its steps. The Market Square by the harbour sells salmon soup, berries and crafts, and the Old Market Hall nearby is a good lunch stop. The centre is compact and flat, so walking is easy. Trams cover the rest.

finland/suomenlinna.name: Suomenlinna sea fortress
finland/suomenlinna.description: An eighteenth-century island fortress, a short ferry ride from Helsinki, a UNESCO site.
finland/suomenlinna.details: Suomenlinna spreads over six islands with bastions, tunnels, museums and picnic spots. The ferry from Market Square takes 15 minutes and is included in city transport tickets. Allow half a day, and bring a layer for the sea breeze.

finland/sauna-design.name: Finnish sauna and design district
finland/sauna-design.description: A public sauna by the sea, plus the design shops and cafes of the Design District.
finland/sauna-design.details: Sauna is central to Finnish life. Loyly and Allas Sea Pool offer public saunas by the harbour, with sea dips in summer and ice swimming in winter. The Design District has galleries and shops. Check whether swimsuits are required, and book evenings ahead.

finland/nuuksio-porvoo.name: Nuuksio National Park or Porvoo old town
finland/nuuksio-porvoo.description: Forest lakes close to the capital, or a red-ochre wooden town on the coast.
finland/nuuksio-porvoo.details: Nuuksio is a national park 40 minutes from Helsinki, with marked trails, lakes and berry picking in summer. Porvoo is a 17th-century town with wooden warehouses on the river, about an hour away. Choose one for a day trip depending on the weather.

finland/turku-castle.name: Turku Castle and the river
finland/turku-castle.description: Finland oldest city with a medieval castle, cathedral and riverside restaurants.
finland/turku-castle.details: Turku Castle dates from the 13th century and holds a museum of Swedish and Finnish history. The cathedral and the Aura River promenade are close. The archipelago to the south is reached by boat in summer. Turku is two hours by train from Helsinki.

finland/tampere.name: Tampere museums and sauna capital
finland/tampere.description: An industrial city turned cultural centre, with museums, lakes and the largest public sauna scene.
finland/tampere.details: Tampere sits between two lakes and has red-brick mills turned into museums, the Moomin Museum and the Rajaportti sauna, Finland oldest public sauna. The Pyynikki ridge has a tower with doughnuts and a view. Trains from Helsinki take about two hours.

finland/savonlinna.name: Savonlinna and Olavinlinna Castle
finland/savonlinna.description: A lake town with a medieval castle on the water, known for its summer opera festival.
finland/savonlinna.details: Olavinlinna is a 15th-century castle on an island in Lake Saimaa. The Savonlinna Opera Festival fills the courtyard with performances in July. Lake cruises explore the Saimaa archipelago, and the area is the home of the rare Saimaa ringed seal.

finland/santa-claus-village.name: Santa Claus Village and the Arctic Circle
finland/santa-claus-village.description: A village on the Arctic Circle where visitors can meet Santa and cross the line.
finland/santa-claus-village.details: Santa Claus Village in Rovaniemi has a post office with an Arctic Circle postmark, reindeer rides and Santa meeting year-round. It is lively in December and quieter in summer. The Arctic Circle line is marked on the ground.

finland/lapland-husky-reindeer.name: Husky and reindeer safari
finland/lapland-husky-reindeer.description: A guided sled ride behind huskies or reindeer through snowy forest (or a summer farm visit).
finland/lapland-husky-reindeer.details: In winter, huskies pull sleds through forest trails and reindeer farms offer sled rides and stories of the Sami herders. Warm outerwear is provided by most operators. In summer, farms offer walks and farm visits. Book ahead for peak winter dates.

finland/northern-lights.name: Northern lights hunt or midnight sun
finland/northern-lights.description: An evening trip into dark skies to look for the aurora from September to March, or the midnight sun in June.
finland/northern-lights.details: The aurora is possible on clear nights from late August to April, with the best chances in the colder months. Guides drive to dark spots away from town and light fires. In summer, the midnight sun allows daylight activity at any hour. Dress in layers, as it is very cold at night.

finland/arktikum-snow.name: Arktikum museum and snow activities
finland/arktikum-snow.description: A museum about Arctic life and nature, plus snowmobiling and snowshoeing in winter.
finland/arktikum-snow.details: The Arktikum in Rovaniemi explains Arctic nature, Sami culture and the polar environment. In winter, snowmobile safaris, snowshoe walks and ice fishing are popular, and some travellers visit a Sami reindeer herder. In summer there are river cruises and hikes.
